checks.purpose: Detect incompatible tools and missing locked build inputs before expensive checks
Validate tasks, decisions, check bindings and archived evidence
Detect generated protocol drift
Validate application boundaries and policy/schema consistency
Check worker and generated Python types
Check worker and generated Python types against Windows stubs from any development host
Exercise protocol, worker and repository-control failure behavior
Validate shared wire fixtures in TypeScript
Typecheck and build the UI
Verify Rust formatting
Test eligible Cargo workspace members, including the portable desktop bridge on non-Windows hosts and the full native desktop tests on Windows x64
Lint all targets in every eligible Cargo workspace member, including native desktop targets
Build the desktop application natively on Windows x64
Search three synthetic instruments in one chart session, switch timeframe and style, and compare visible partial and final updates against the frozen history and selected subscription.
Verify real A/B/clear chart selection, local AI chart mutation admission, independent revision conflicts, authorized exactly-once replay, rollback, undo and fresh writer reconnect.

Exercise the shared registry and chart adapter with independent declarative preview values, trusted sample sessions and missing buckets, unverified CSV continuity, warm-up, cancellation, failure isolation, immutable CSV acceptance, removal, restart and source revocation.
Verify explicit local approval for each trusted Python run, frozen synthetic input, exact output, cancellation and validation, CSV purpose denial and immutable restoration without recomputation.
Verify the human-AI tool workflow and its authorization boundaries
Verify a packaged clean-machine Windows installation
Verify performance, bounded memory and process cleanup
Verify configured secret storage, redaction and worker exposure boundaries
Validate fixed synthetic market data semantics and expected bars
Verify closed-bar repair and unresolved gaps on the ordinary chart through the real worker, including frozen history and rejection of invalid or interrupted repairs.

Run the full SQLite persistence suite against populated v1 through v8 predecessors, transaction interruption and recovery, preserved workspace, note and frozen folder lineage, additive layout storage, isolated profiles, logical backups, deletion and WAL cleanup, and rejection of archive-supplied approval or outbound authority. Real model and Windows UI acceptance have separate checks.
Replay context, authorization, cancellation and claim-grounding scenarios with versioned inputs
Validate installer identity, retained native evidence, notices and observed owner product review
Validate locked dependency and license inventory, reviewed immutable Actions, and fresh advisory disposition with target scope guards
Verify offline snapshot diagnostics and bounded observed-price aggregation using synthetic counterexamples
Exercise opt-in historical chart, real Rust/Python read operations and browser selection/error behavior; excludes live recovery and packaged desktop execution
Exercise the local development entry in a clean Chromium session, verify synthetic history through the loopback endpoint and enforce its read-only scope

Exercise local CSV selection intent, cancellation, explicit mapping, and stock and futures previews in the built UI with a synthetic Tauri invoke substitute. Native dialog behavior and durable import require separate evidence.

Exercise the built UI through the profile-bound Rust desktop state, complete-file normalization, SQLite and the chart adapter. Verify a publication above the preview row limit, retry, held rows, and a changed single-file revision. After restart and source removal, inspect the exact raw fields of a quoted multiline record outside the preview, and verify profile scope, stale selections and display-right removal. The test supplies the selected directory through a synthetic picker.

Exercise folder review and guarded publication through the built UI, Rust registry, Python checker and SQLite. Observe additions, all alias locators, competing prices, explicit unit, adjustment and venue contradictions, incomplete coverage and discarded late replies. Publish with explicit source and bar withdrawals, recover a lost reply, and reopen and revoke frozen folder revisions after restart.
Verify the native SQLite v7 migration over populated v6, frozen lineage, source-qualified locators, original byte reuse, scoped retry, and transactional rollback and recovery.

Exercise checked folder admission, editable stock and futures mappings, raw-only quotes, source lineage, idempotent refresh and schema drift through the built UI, Rust registry, Python parser and SQLite. Verify reviewed conflict choices, withdrawals, interrupted publication and frozen source row reads. The harness supplies a synthetic path to the trusted folder chooser callback. Native Windows shell selection and WebView2 remain separate observations.

Exercise keyboard and declarative edits and the real chart and panels through the private workspace bridge and SQLite. Verify revision and preview guards, exactly-once retry, undo, reset, same-profile reopen, simulated sample restoration, and frozen CSV disconnection and revocation with separately enforced access. This browser check is not native WebView2 acceptance.

Independently verify model and data selection, declared capabilities, transmission scope, contrary evidence, corrections and tool outcomes in an authorized real text session. Record provider, route, model and observed charges where available. Check ordinary connected turns and exact per-request private excerpts at the actual connector. Report the observed local or cloud deployment.
Observe one explicitly authorized real duplex voice session, mixed-language entity correction, visible tool results, cancellation and text continuity.

Exercise a local MCP session against the running desktop core using bounded synthetic chart data. Verify visible attribution, grant and entitlement filtering, idempotent annotation, concurrent edits, undo and revocation.

Observe an authorized Codex CLI session and a compatible desktop AI client on supported hosts using the delivered local bridge. Check the same open chart, attributed annotations, denied operations and undo.
Exercise explicit synthetic replay through the ordinary development chart, loopback bridge, shared registry and market worker, including selection cancellation, a visible gap and final canvas update.
Exercise the chart with real frozen normal, stale, gapped and empty sample reads, independent session and freshness states, delayed selection, distinct typed failures and retry.
Validate the retained actual Ubuntu-local integrated workspace observation, offline journeys and external-session disposition.
Validate the physical Windows dual-boot native WebView2 session, inputs, observed actions, OS build, screenshots and source revision.
Observe an authorized real market source, specific route, dataset revision and permitted use.
Exercise the ordinary chart and real worker through an owned process exit, verified resumption, a single logical subscription and preserved frozen history.

Verify one real loopback futures baseline and use its frozen synthetic reads for injected recovery, rejection and cancellation. Check real stock replacement and startup terminal diagnostics separately.

Verify profile-local decision notes and v1 through v3 migrations. Exercise confirmation, replay, deletion, complete backup capacity, stage expiry and disposal, marker union, and rollback when killed before commit.
Verify profile-local private records, body-free replay, revision and authorization gates, backup recovery, tombstone union and migration rollback.

Exercise the real opted-in local writer through browser and process restart, timeframe undo, terminal cleanup, decision-note confirmation, deletion, backup and restore, private-record lifecycle and stale approval, and chart evidence selection and narrow projection of actual frozen profile data.
Exercise the built desktop UI with substituted Tauri IPC for default startup, authorized timeframe and undo, and rejection. The portable Rust bridge checks exercise the actual registry and storage.

Exercise local text settings and explicit offline mock, OpenAI credential entry and ordinary-text disclosure, ordinary turns, bounded selected-chart tool calls, corrected and denied intervals, and pending-reply invalidation through the Rust registry and real Ollama adapter against an owned synthetic HTTP peer. Verify that the browser guard allows local route removal and blocks and reports a different loopback origin. Hold a real published CSV status read while changing the workspace source and distinguish pre-admission rejection, accepted writes, superseding revisions and lost acknowledgements using synthetic profiles.
Replay profile, actor, disclosure, context isolation, credential revision, expiry, duplicate send and cancellation boundaries without using a provider or opening a storage transaction.

Capture the final fixed-destination OpenAI Responses HTTPS requests for two reconstructed turns with synthetic credentials and an isolated TLS peer. Verify redacted authorization failure, local denial and redirect rejection without a real account.

acceptance.requirement: A clean Windows x64 system without Python/Node can install and run simulated mode
Open all three synthetic instruments and switch timeframes; the UI explicitly displays simulated
After disconnecting the market worker, its status is visible and recovery uses bounded retries without duplicate subscriptions
Mock AI creates a declarative abnormal-volatility indicator based on user requirements; preview, acceptance, removal, and undo all complete
AI tools and user operations use the same registry; direct requests for unauthorized operations are rejected
For new work, existing confirmations become invalid when parameters, the code hash or a bound workspace or selection revision changes
Indicator timeouts, exceptions, and invalid output neither interrupt market data nor overwrite accepted indicators
Closing and reopening restores the workspace and indicator versions without re-executing previous AI tasks
Logs, the database, and worker environments contain no plaintext credentials
No worker child processes remain alive after application shutdown
Generated types have no uncommitted differences; schemas and validation in all three languages are consistent
Select a local CSV directory, correct an import preview and refresh it with new files. Source revisions and rejected records are inspectable and repeat imports are idempotent.
Preview, apply, name, restore and revert a single-chart layout. Manual and AI edits use the same panel settings, linked selections and allowed interactions.
The human and AI can each point to a versioned workspace object, reveal evidence in another panel, refine the selection and return to the previous view.
AI operations show their target, preview or progress and actual outcome in the affected view. Confirmation, denial, failure and cancellation remain visible.
An explicitly enabled real voice session supports spoken discussion, interruption and text follow-up under the same operation permissions. A denied or interrupted request has an observable outcome.

Starting from a buy question, compare evidence, revise a challenged premise, and perform only a separately authorized workspace change. Reopen a user-saved decision and distinguish the original rationale from the later outcome.

Choose a provider and model independently of market data. Show verified capabilities, destination and applicable charges, handle an unsupported feature, and exercise a configured model on an evidence-based discussion.

An opted-in local MCP client reads the selected chart and, with a write grant, adds a reversible annotation to the same open workspace. The UI attributes the action. Denied, stale and revoked requests preserve the workspace and respect output permissions.
Observe Codex CLI and one compatible desktop AI client separately reading the open chart and applying a scoped annotation. Verify the visible result and undo on each supported test host.
